# Project title update does not appear in app state

## What was being attempted

Set the project title to Alex Morgan — Strategy & Growth Consultant after completing the consultant website.

## Context

Single-page Elements project; home page title is Alex Morgan — Strategy & Growth Consultant and filename is index.html.

## What was tried

1. Called updateProjectSettings with the desired title during initial setup.
2. Repeated updateProjectSettings after final validation.
3. Repeated it again immediately before recordPageSync; every call reported success.

## Expected behaviour

updateProjectSettings should change the siteSettings title shown in the live app state.

## Actual behaviour

The tool repeatedly returned updated:[title], but the latest app state still reports siteSettings.title as My Website. The page title, browser title and SEO metadata are correct.

## Recommendations

1. Verify whether siteSettings.title maps to a different writable field than getProjectSettings/updateProjectSettings title.
2. Return the effective site title after writes or warn when the UI state did not change.

---
title: Project Knowledge
summary: Index of all project knowledge pages
---

This is the AI-maintained knowledge base for this project, following the Karpathy compiled-knowledge pattern. The LLM reads live pages once and compiles them into an interlinked graph of notes. Subsequent sessions read the notes, not the live pages — answers compound rather than being re-derived each time.

## Note graph

The knowledge graph lives in four folders. Use `[[folder/note]]` wikilinks for cross-references between notes.

- **pages/** — one note per live RapidWeaver page; keyed on `pageId`; records purpose, sections, components, and summary in the user's voice
- **concepts/** — themes and patterns spanning multiple pages (e.g. "testimonials pattern", "pricing section")
- **entities/** — people, clients, tools, custom components, publishing destinations
- **analyses/** — durable answers to synthesis questions; filed when a query answer is worth preserving

### When to create a concept or entity note

Create a note proactively — do not wait to be asked:

- **entities/**: any named person appearing in a role (officer, winner, organiser, contact); any named event, race, trophy, award, or external tool/service.
- **concepts/**: any structural or content pattern that appears across 3 or more pages (e.g. same image+link layout, recurring winner table structure, recurring membership pricing model).

Use a lowercase hyphenated slug (e.g. `entities/ian-wright.md`, `concepts/photo-album-pattern.md`). Add a `## See also` section with `[[folder/note]]` wikilinks back to every page note that references it, and add the reciprocal link in each of those page notes.

### Page note format

```yaml
---
title: Page Title
type: page          # page | concept | entity | analysis
pageId: <uuid>      # for type:page — the Elements page UUID (stable across sessions)
path: /slug         # site path
lastIngested: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ
sources: []         # [[links]] to notes this draws from
tags: []
concerns:           # known problems, tech debt, or gotchas for this page/concept
  - "Brief description of the issue (severity: low|medium|high)"
---

# Page Title

Summary in the user's voice. Sections, components used, index/sitemap flags.

**Build mechanics** (required — record HOW things are built, not just WHAT they render): list the element types used, any custom components and how many instances, whether data is hardcoded or driven by CMS/properties, and whether styling uses design-system tokens or bypasses them (e.g. "12 per-year hand-edited HTML custom components; data hardcoded in template; colours bypass Tailwind tokens").

## See also
- [[concepts/related-concept]]
- [[entities/entity-name]]
```

## Design System

- **[style-writing.md](style-writing.md)** — voice and tone guide; read via `getDesignSystem` before authoring copy
- **[style-visual.md](style-visual.md)** — layout and visual conventions; read via `getDesignSystem` before building pages

## Project admin

- **[overview.md](overview.md)** — site purpose, target audience, and high-level structure
- **[journal.md](journal.md)** — append-only session log (newest entries at top)
- **[concerns.md](concerns.md)** — known problems, tech debt, gotchas, and fragile areas (derived from per-note `concerns:` frontmatter + `lintKnowledge`; regenerated on close)
- **[backlog.md](backlog.md)** — outstanding work and speculative ideas with priority and status
- **[services.md](services.md)** — external services, APIs, and integrations
- **[field-reports/](field-reports/)** — structured AI session blocker reports; summaries linked from concerns.md

## Operations

Three recurring workflows — all orchestrated by the LLM using the storage primitives above.

**Ingest** (triggered by drift or new page): `getPageMarkdown(pageId)` → `editKnowledge` writePage `pages/<slug>.md` with `pageId` + `lastIngested` → touch/create linked `concepts/` and `entities/` notes → add `[[folder/note]]` wikilinks both directions and `## See also` → refresh `index.md`. If the page reveals a new voice or visual convention, call `updateDesignSystem` to reconcile the design guides.

**Query**: read `index.md` → relevant notes (re-ingest only if `stale: true`) → synthesise with `[[folder/note]]` wikilinks as citations → optionally file durable answer as `analyses/<slug>.md`. **Exception — architecture/improvement requests**: for any "how do I improve", "review", or "what's wrong with" question, always inspect the live document first (`listCustomComponents` + a sample `getCustomComponent` + `getPageContent` on representative pages) before answering, regardless of note freshness. Rank findings by altitude: maintainability/structure → design-system → content. Record findings into per-note `concerns:` and regenerate `concerns.md`.

**Lint**: call `lintKnowledge` → act on orphans, broken links, stale notes, dangling page notes, index drift → fix and log.

## Purpose

Present [[entities/alex-morgan]] as a premium independent strategy and growth consultant and convert qualified founders, CEOs and leadership teams into consultation enquiries.

## Target Audience

Founder-led businesses, growing companies, established organisations entering a new phase, and senior leadership teams facing an important strategic decision.

## Structure

A single-page website at [[pages/home]]. Navigation jumps to About, Expertise, Approach, Results and Contact sections. The page combines editorial photography, oversized serif statements, restrained service and process layouts, credibility content, biography and a final consultation CTA.

## Design Intent

Sophisticated and editorial: warm ivory and stone backgrounds, deep olive and taupe sections, muted clay accents, serif display typography, clean sans-serif body text, generous whitespace and minimal decoration.

## See also
- [[pages/home]]
- [[entities/alex-morgan]]
- [[style-writing]]
- [[style-visual]]

---
title: Writing Style
summary: Voice and tone guide — read before authoring any copy
---

## Voice & Tone

Intelligent, confident, calm, experienced, approachable and direct. Premium without being grandiose. Avoid corporate jargon, hype and generic transformation claims.

## Sentence Rhythm

Use clear declarative sentences, varied between short emphatic statements and measured explanatory paragraphs. Keep paragraphs narrow and concise. Use three-part phrasing sparingly for emphasis.

## Vocabulary

Prefer: clarity, decisions, priorities, perspective, strategy, growth, leadership, practical, deliberate, sustainable. Avoid: unlock your potential, game-changing, cutting-edge, leverage, synergise, world-class.

## Person & POV

First-person singular for Alex’s expertise and working style. Address the reader directly when discussing their challenges.

## Heading Style

Sentence case. Major headings are concise editorial statements, often with a measured contrast or question. Avoid excessive title case and exclamation marks.

## Caption & Label Style

Section labels use short uppercase phrases with wide tracking. Buttons are direct sentence-case actions. Navigation labels are single words where possible.

## See also
- [[style-visual]]
- [[pages/home]]
- [[entities/alex-morgan]]

---
title: Visual Style
summary: Layout and visual conventions — read before building or restructuring pages
---

## Layout Patterns

| Pattern | Description | Pages |
|---------|-------------|-------|
| Immersive hero | Full-viewport editorial image with dark overlay, minimal overlaid navigation and lower-left copy | Home |
| Editorial statement | Centred narrow serif statement with generous vertical whitespace | Home |
| Split image and copy | Edge-to-edge two-column composition, stacking naturally on smaller screens | Home |
| Typographic service rows | Unboxed columns separated by hairline rules | Home |
| Image interlude | Cinematic full-width photograph with minimal pull-line | Home |
| Numbered process | Three wide typographic stages with oversized numbers | Home |
| Pull quote | Oversized serif quotation without a card | Home |

## Colour Palette

| Role | Value |
|------|-------|
| Primary dark | Olive 800–900 |
| Accent dark | Taupe 700 |
| Main background | Stone 50 |
| Secondary background | Stone 100–200 |
| Text | Stone 700–900 |
| Small accent | Muted orange 700 |

## Typography

| Role | Font | Size / Weight |
|------|------|---------------|
| Display headings | Quote serif | 4xl–8xl, regular |
| Body and navigation | Body sans | Base–xl, regular/medium |
| Labels | Body sans | Small, medium, widely tracked |

## Spacing & Rhythm

Use large section padding: 20 tokens on mobile and 28–32 on tablet/desktop. Maintain narrow body-copy measures between 560px and 760px. Prefer open layouts, generous gaps and hairline dividers over cards, shadows or decorative effects.

## Image Treatment

Large editorial photography with natural light, warm muted grading and architectural context. Portraits use a 4:5 crop; cinematic interludes use 70–82vh. Avoid corporate stock-photo clichés.

## Navigation Structure

Minimal header over the hero. Full navigation appears at large breakpoints; the consultation CTA remains visible. Single-page links target major section containers. Footer repeats navigation, contact and social links.

## Responsive Behaviour

Mobile-first single columns. Two-column editorial sections switch at large screens; service grid moves from one to two to four columns; process and statistics become three columns at medium screens. Display typography scales at medium and large breakpoints.
